title: The query planner: Catalyst, predicate pushdown and column pruning

videos.script: When you write a DataFrame or a SQL query, you say what you want. Not how to get it. {{what}} The how belongs to Catalyst, Spark's planner. It turns your query into four plans, one after the other, and only the last one runs. {{plans}} Along the way it moves your filters down to the files, drops the columns you never use, and picks the join. {{rules}} This lesson reads those plans, and then measures what they save. One day out of three hundred and sixty-five, read by opening one file. {{prune}} And then the same question, asked through a Python function, opening all of them. Same answer. The planner simply could not see. {{blind}} Last, a plan that changes while it runs. Two hundred partitions planned, a handful used, because Spark looked at the real data and changed its mind. {{aqe}}
